title: Imaging-Guided Bioreactor for Generating Bioengineered Airway Tissue
protocol: Create a computer-aided design (CAD) model of the bioreactor chamber using CAD generator software.
Export the CAD model to CNC controller software.
Cut the polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) plastic using a CNC machine to create the bioreactor chamber.
Sterilize all bioreactor components, such as Luer adapters and screws.
Assemble all bioreactor components to the main tissue culture chamber in a clean environment.
Insert a tube lens into a stackable lens tube and secure it using a retaining ring.
Mount the lens-tube assembly onto a scientific CMOS camera via a C-mount adapter.
Use software such as Micro-Manager to operate the camera and acquire photos and videos.
Aim an object located at a long distance from the camera (e.g., 10 m) and adjust the distance between the tube lens and imaging sensor until a focused image is formed on the computer screen.
Mount a filter lens on a dual-edge super-resolution dichroic mirror and a laser to the device using optical cage system components, including assembly rod, threaded cage plate, and cage cube.
Connect an objective lens (20x) to the device.
Mount a GRIN lens (diameter = 500 µm) at the distal end of the lens tube via the XY translator.
Adjust the distance between the GRIN lens and the objective lens to form focused microscopic images.
Sanitize the surgical area and sterilize the surgical instruments using an autoclave at 121 °C for 30 min prior to surgery.
Place a rat in the induction chamber and deliver 2.5% of isoflurane for 15 min using a small vaporizer to anesthetize the animal.
Assess the anesthesia depth by firmly pinching the toe and confirming that the animal does not respond to the toe pinch.
Administer 1 mL of 1,000 unit/mL heparin through the lateral tail vein.
Expose the animal to 5% isoflurane for an additional 15-20 min to euthanize it.
Place the animal on the surgical board in a face-up supine position.
Fix the rat on the surgical board by immobilizing the legs and tail using adhesive tape.
Sterilize the rat's neck and chest regions using 70% isopropyl alcohol (IPA).
Make a 3-4 cm incision in the skin to open the abdominal cavity carefully.
Transect the inferior vena cava (IVC) using scissors.
Confirm euthanasia by exsanguination.
Perform an incision in the midline of the neck and expose the trachea for tracheotomy.
Perform a midline thoracotomy by making an incision in the chest wall and cutting between the ribs to reach the trachea end connected to the lung.
Use bicep and scissors to cut both ends of the trachea and isolate it.
Rinse the isolated trachea using 20 mL of 1x phosphate-buffered saline (1x PBS).
Transfer the rinsed trachea to the bioreactor using sterilized biceps.
Secure the two ends of the trachea to the Luer connector using a 4-0 suture thread.
Deliver 5 mL of culture medium to the bioreactor chamber using a programmable syringe pump at a flow rate of 5 mL/min.
Tightly close the bioreactor lid with an acrylic plastic lid and screws.
Close the bioreactor chamber tubing connections with male/female Luer plugs.
Place the bioreactor on the imaging stage for visualization.
Prepare carboxyfluorescein succinimidyl ester (CFSE) solution at a concentration of 100 μM in the CFSE cell labeling kit by diluting it with 1x PBS.
Infuse 500 µL of the CFSE solution through the trachea via the syringe pump at a flow rate of 5 mL/min.
Wait for 10 min after stopping the pump.
Wash the trachea lumen by infusing 10 mL of 1x PBS using the syringe pump.
Insert the distal imaging end of the GRIN lens into the trachea via the Luer connector attached to one end of the trachea.
Gently move the GRIN lens inside the trachea until the trachea surface is focused.
Take photos and videos in bright-field or fluorescence at 20x magnification.
Introduce white light through the cage cube to illuminate the trachea lumen.
Click on the Live icon to show the luminal surface of the trachea in real-time.
Use Imaging Setting > Exposure (ms) to change exposure time to the desired value.
Adjust the contrast and brightness of images using the Histogram and Intensity Scaling window or Auto Stretch option.
Click on the Snap icon to freeze the image.
Use Setting > Export Images as Displaced to save the images in the desired format.
Alternatively, use Setting > ImageJ to directly export the image to the ImageJ software and save it.
Illuminate the trachea lumen with CFSE-specific laser light (excitation wavelength: 488 nm, emission wavelength: 515 nm).
Acquire images following steps 3.5.2-3.5.3.
Remove the GRIN lens gently from the trachea.
Prepare a 2% sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) decellularization solution in distilled water.
Instill 50 µL of SDS through the trachea at a flow rate of 6.3 mL/min using a syringe pump and trachea cannula.
Close bioreactor tubing connections with male/female Luer plugs.
Transfer the bioreactor to an incubator.
Allow SDS to dwell within the trachea for 10 min at 37 °C.
Instill another 50 µL of SDS solution through the trachea.
Incubate for 10 min.
Irrigate the trachea lumen with 500 µL of 1x PBS via syringe pump at a flow rate of 10 mL/min for three cycles.

Place the bioreactor on a shaker and mechanically vibrate the bioreactor at 20 Hz frequency and displacement amplitude of approximately 0.3 mm to promote detachment of SDS-treated epithelial cells from the trachea lumen.
Instill 500 µL of 1x PBS twice through the trachea lumen while it is being mechanically vibrated to remove residual SDS and cell debris.
Evaluate clearance of the epithelial layer by measuring the intensity of CFSE using the GRIN lens imaging device.
Perform hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining, trichrome, pentachrome, and immunostaining to confirm epithelium removal.
Remove the trachea from the bioreactor.
Fix the trachea in 30 mL of 4% neutral buffered paraformaldehyde solution in 1x PBS at 4 °C overnight.
Wash the fixed trachea with 10 mL of 1x PBS.
Transfer the washed trachea to 30 mL of 70% alcohol and keep it at 4 °C overnight.
Cut the trachea into small cylindrical sections (~5 mm).
Insert the tissue sections in tissue embedding cassettes (length x width x height: 4 cm x 2.5 cm x 0.5 cm).
Keep two trachea sections in each cassette.
Dehydrate the tissue sections in a series of isopropyl alcohol solutions - 85%, 90%, 95%, and 100% - for 1 h in 30 mL of each solution.
Submerge the cassettes in clearing agent (e.g., xylene) for 2 h to displace IPA from the tissue sections completely.
Submerge the cassettes in paraffin for 2 h.
Embed the cassettes in paraffin at 4 °C overnight.
Cut the paraffin-embedded tissues into thin sections (5-8 μm) using a microtome device for H&E, trichrome, pentachrome, and immunostaining.
Fix the trachea in 30 mL of 2.5% glutaraldehyde solution in 1x PBS (pH = 7.4) at 4 °C overnight.
Rinse the trachea tissue with 10 mL of 1x PBS.
Cut the trachea tissue longitudinally into small semi-cylinder sections (length: ~5 mm).
Insert the tissue sections in the cassettes.
Dehydrate the sections in a series of IPA solutions - 35%, 50%, 70%, 85%, 95%, and 100% - for 10 min in 30 mL of each solution.
Remove the previous solution before adding the next solution.
Submerge the tissues in 100% IPA: HMDS (2:1; v/v) for 10 min.
Submerge the tissues in 100% IPA: HMDS (1:2; v/v) for 10 min.
Submerge the tissues in 100% HMDS overnight.
Remove the tissues from the HMDS solution and allow them to dry under a fume hood for 1 h.
Mount the tissue section on aluminum pin stubs using carbon double-sided conductive tape or silver conductive paste.
Thaw frozen mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) for 30 s in a 37 °C water bath.
Count mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) using a hemocytometer.
Prepare a cell solution with a concentration of 5 x 10^6 cells/mL.
Label the cells fluorescently by incubating them with 2 mL of CFSE solution at room temperature for 15 min.
Rinse the cells three times with 5 mL of 1x PBS.
Resuspend the cells in fresh culture medium to a final concentration of 3 x 10^7 cells/mL.
Prepare hydrogel pre-gel solution as per manufacturer's instructions using collagen I.
Mix one part of chilled neutralization solution with nine parts of rat tail collagen for collagen pre-gel preparation.
Gently pipette the mixture up and down for adequate mixing.
Add mesenchymal stem cells to the prepared hydrogel solution at a desired concentration (e.g., 5 x 10^6 cells/mL).
Mix the cells and gel solution gently using a micropipette.
Attach one end of the trachea to a programmable syringe pump through a Luer connector.
Deliver 5 mL of fresh culture medium at 37 °C into the bioreactor chamber using the syringe pump at a flow rate of 5 mL/min.

Administer a 10 µL bolus of the cell-hydrogel mixture into the de-epithelialized trachea within the bioreactor using the syringe pump at a flow rate of 5 mL/min to generate a cell-hydrogel layer on the trachea lumen.
Place the bioreactor in a sterile cell culture incubator at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for gelation.
Sterilize the GRIN lens by wiping with 70% IPA or ethanol.
Place the bioreactor on the imaging stage to visualize the distribution of implanted cells.
Take photos and videos in both bright-field and fluorescent modes as needed.
Infuse 1 mL of culture medium into the trachea lumen using a syringe pump at a flow rate of 1 mL/min.
Culture the cell-seeded trachea within the bioreactor in an incubator at 37 °C for the desired time.
Refresh the culture medium in the trachea lumen and the bioreactor chamber every 24 h for long-term culture.
Keep the media inside the lumen static and change it every 24 h during cell culture.
Perfuse the media outside the trachea continuously via a unidirectional flow at 5 mL/min during cell culture.
Remove the trachea from the bioreactor after culturing for a certain time period (e.g., 1 and 4 days in this study).
Cut the trachea longitudinally into two semi-cylinder sections on days 1 and 4 of in vitro culture to expose inner surfaces.
Use a conventional fluorescent microscope with a FITC filter to visualize CFSE-labeled cells in fluorescence mode.
Acquire images using Micro-Manager software following steps 3.5 and 3.6.
Open an image in ImageJ software and convert the image to a binary image (16-bit) using Image > Type > 16-bit.
Set the image scale with the scale bar using Analyze > Set Scale.
Analyze the images taken by the fluorescent microscope and calculate cell densities on upper and lower sections using ImageJ software.
Adjust the threshold of the image to highlight the structures of the cells using Image > Adjust > Threshold.
Use Analyze > Analyze Particles to count the number of cells.
Calculate the density of the cells by dividing the number of cells by the surface area of the image.
Incubate trachea tissue and the cells in the bioreactor at 37 °C for 6 h.
Stain the cells with 4 mM calcein-AM and 2 mM ethidium homodimer-1 in 1 mL of 1x PBS at room temperature for 15 min.
Rinse the cells with 1x PBS.
Visualize the cells using a fluorescent microscope.
Count the live and dead cells as described in step 5.12.
Calculate cell viability as the percentage of live cells (stained with calcein-AM) per total cells (both live and dead cells).
